title: How memory works
examples: What is the difference between short-term and long-term memory?
Why do I forget things I learn in school?
Is it true that studying a little bit every day is better than cramming?

explain.say: Today we are learning how your amazing memory system works.
Short-term memory holds information for a short time only.
Long-term memory stores information for much longer periods of time.
Forgetting happens because memories fade or are hard to get back.
Spaced practice means studying over many short sessions.

draw.text: Spaced Practice: Spreading out study time

explain.say: In real life, remembering a new phone number needs practice over days.

draw.text: Real Life: Learning a phone number

faq.q: Why is it better to study a little bit every day?
faq.a: This is because spaced practice helps move information into your long-term memory. It strengthens the memory pathways over time.
asks: Does cramming really hurt my memory?
What is the best way to keep information long-term?

faq.q: What is the difference between short-term and long-term memory?
faq.a: Short-term memory holds things you are thinking about right now, like a phone number you just heard. Long-term memory holds things you learn permanently, like your name.
asks: Where does my brain keep my permanent memories?
Is short-term memory like a notepad?

faq.q: Why do I forget things I learn in school?
faq.a: Forgetting is normal; some memories fade away if we do not practice retrieving them. Repetition and linking new ideas help stop that fading.
asks: Can I stop myself from forgetting things?

faq.q: Does the brain get stronger with practice?
faq.a: Yes, just like muscles, your brain gets stronger when you challenge it with new information. This process is called neural strengthening.
asks: Is learning a language good for my brain?

faq.a: Encoding is the process of taking new information and turning it into a format your brain can store. You can use pictures or stories to help encode.
asks: How do I make memories stick?
What is the first step to remembering something?

facts: Short-term memory has a limited capacity for holding information.
Long-term memory can store vast amounts of information indefinitely.
Retrieval failure means you know the information but cannot access it right now.
Spaced practice combats the natural forgetting curve of memory.

quiz.say: If you read a list of five words and then try to recall them an hour later, which memory system are you primarily using?
quiz.why: Because an hour is a relatively long time, the memory needs to be stored beyond the immediate working space.

wrong.0: Sensory memory only holds information for a fraction of a second.
wrong.1: Working memory is more about manipulating information than long-term storage.
wrong.3: Short-term memory usually only holds information for seconds or minutes.

quiz.say: To improve your memory for a historical date, which study technique is most effective?

options.show: Telling a friend the date once
options.say: Telling a friend the date once

options.show: Reviewing the date over several days
options.say: Reviewing the date over several days

options.show: Reading the chapter five times in one night
options.say: Reading the chapter five times in one night

options.show: Drawing a picture of the date
options.say: Drawing a picture of the date

quiz.why: This method is spaced practice, which strengthens the memory trace over time.

wrong.0: Telling it once is just one retrieval attempt, not spaced practice.
wrong.2: This is called cramming, which leads to quick forgetting.
wrong.3: While drawing helps encoding, it is not the primary method for spaced review.
